components.name: Worksheet
components.purpose: Method frame (board Worksheet / old-feed LineInput): the student writes each calculation line and the engine checks it against the step's expected solution graph; the default for every 'calculer / montrer que' question.
components.student_action: type lines with the math keys and number tiles; tap an earlier line to fix it
components.engine_needs: src/method line chains (lineChain, exprLine, mutations) plus one new solution-graph template per 3se question type (continuity, limits, asymptotes, symmetry, derivative, sequences, dot product, determinants, complex forms, counting, statistics)
components.props_sketch: frame type 'lines': graph {template, params}, variables (x, n, m, t, a, b), tiles
components.extends_note: 3se lines need what the parser and line engine lack today: (1) complex numbers (constant i, NumberSystem for a + bi) for T2_CH04; (2) vectors / coordinate triples and dot products as line items (vec(AB)(2, -1, 2), u.v) for T2_CH01/05/06/07; (3) equation, inequality and equivalence lines (=, <, <=, <=>) and inequality chains (0 <= |wn - 3| <= 5/(n + 1)), with solution sets and 'k in Z' families; (4) partie entiere E(x); (5) parameters (m, a, b, k, t) judged on samples of the parameter too; (6) exact display of surds (2 sqrt 7, 6 sqrt 21 / 7) and multiples of pi

notes_by_year.3se: 3se lines need what the parser and line engine lack today: (1) complex numbers (constant i, NumberSystem for a + bi) for T2_CH04; (2) vectors / coordinate triples and dot products as line items (vec(AB)(2, -1, 2), u.v) for T2_CH01/05/06/07; (3) equation, inequality and equivalence lines (=, <, <=, <=>) and inequality chains (0 <= |wn - 3| <= 5/(n + 1)), with solution sets and 'k in Z' families; (4) partie entiere E(x); (5) parameters (m, a, b, k, t) judged on samples of the parameter too; (6) exact display of surds (2 sqrt 7, 6 sqrt 21 / 7) and multiples of pi
notes_by_year.2sc: Beyond the 3se list (inequality / equivalence lines, parameters, exact surds and pi multiples, vectors, complex numbers): (1) radicals: sqrt(p - q sqrt r) simplified, conjugate to clear a denominator, sqrt(u^2) = |u|; (2) absolute values |x - a| removed by sign; (3) encadrement lines (2.236 < sqrt5 < 2.237 => 0.236 < t < 0.237) checked bound by bound, 'valeur approchee par defaut / par exces', rounding; (4) percentages, coefficients multiplicateurs, indices base 100, scientific notation; (5) integers written with digit letters (6a3b) and division statements N = dq + r; (6) plane vectors as symbols vec(AB): Chasles rewriting, linear combinations in a base (vec(AB), vec(AC)), components and det(u, v); (7) cartesian equations of lines and circles and a 3x3 linear system by elimination; (8) arithmetic and geometric sums n(a + b)/2 and a(1 - q^n)/(1 - q); (9) money rounded to the millime
notes_by_year.1s: beyond the 3se and 2eme notes (inequality / equivalence lines, surds, pi, vectors as symbols with Chasles, components, encadrements, percentages, scientific notation, N = dq + r, systems by elimination): (1) angles in degrees as quantities (angle ADB = 180 - 80 - 30 = 70); (2) named lengths and angles of the current figure as symbols bound to engine values (AN = (3/4) x 8 = 6; cos ABC = BH / AB), so a line about the figure is judged without coordinates on screen; (3) synthetic vector lines (vec(ED) = vec(EC) + vec(CD) = 2 vec(AB), vec(GA) + vec(GB) + vec(GC) = 0) judged on several random instances of the figure, as check_ch01 / check_ch05 do; (4) prime-power products (2^2 x 3^3 x 7) kept factored for PGCD / PPCM lines; (5) the long-division step 90 = 14 x 6 + 6 written as a line

components.name: CardsPick
components.purpose: Method frame: pick one of 2-5 sentence cards giving the reason, rule or claim behind a step ('polynome donc continue', 'terme de plus haut degre', 'orthogonal a deux vecteurs non colineaires').

components.engine_needs: card evaluators (src/method/cards.ts, claims.ts); new claim kinds per chapter
components.props_sketch: frame type 'cards': cards [{id, text}], evaluator

components.name: PlanCards
components.purpose: Method frame: order 3-5 plan cards of a multi-step argument (continuity on R: pieces then junction; existence then uniqueness; plan d'etude of a function).
components.student_action: order the cards, confirm
components.engine_needs: checkPlan (any order respecting what each card uses)
components.props_sketch: frame type 'plan': cards [{id, text, uses[]}]

components.name: NumericTwin
components.purpose: Pick values for the letter(s) and see both sides of an identity agree before proving it (1 - f(x) = (x - 1)^2/(x^2 + 1), cos 3x = 4cos^3 x - 3cos x, f(x) = ax + b + c/(x - 2)).
components.student_action: tap values, compare both sides
components.engine_needs: safe parser evaluates both sides at each value (exists); exact values for pi-multiples and surds
components.props_sketch: symbols (1-2 letters), template, compare, values (numbers or 'pi/12', 'sqrt(2)')

components.name: PredictReveal

components.name: StatementTap

components.engine_needs: none (targets in content)
components.props_sketch: frame type 'read': sentence, targets

components.name: CounterexampleHunt
components.purpose: 'Try to break this claim': the student proposes x, n or a bound M against a 'for all' statement (f(x) <= 1, d(x) >= 2, tan x >= x, g has a maximum, (An) is bounded) and the engine says whether the claim survives or is broken (local max 1 beaten by f(4) = 17).
components.student_action: type or drag a trial value, submit tries, then pick 'holds' or 'fails'
components.engine_needs: claim = inequality between two content expressions on a domain, or 'has a maximum' / 'is bounded above'; exact evaluation at the tried value; the true answer known from the analysis / sequences engine (sup, max, limit) so the final pick is graded; for 'bounded above' the engine returns an n with An > M
components.props_sketch: claim {kind: le | ge | has_max | bounded_above, lhs, rhs, domain}, variable, maxTries, hintValues

components.name: CompareTwo

components.engine_needs: none of its own
components.props_sketch: left, right (inner specs), leftLabel, rightLabel, insight

components.name: IntervalBuilder
components.purpose: Write a domain or a solution set by building it on a number line (open / closed ends, unions, isolated points, excluded values); the written form ]-inf, -4] U [2, +inf[ builds itself.
components.student_action: tap endpoints on the line (chips of allowed values), toggle bracket ends, add a piece or a point, choose +-infinity
components.engine_needs: new src/engine/intervals.ts: exact endpoints (fractions, surds, multiples of pi), union normalisation, set equality with the engine's set (domain of a content expression, solution of an inequality, or a given set), localized feedback (wrong end, wrong bracket, missing piece)

components.name: ProductGrid
components.purpose: The 'generic rectangle' for products of polynomials: each term of one factor times each term of the other fills a cell, cells of the same degree share a colour and are collected into the expanded form; used to expand (sqrt5 - 1)^2, to identify unknown coefficients (P(x) = (x - 3)(mx^2 + nx + p)), to read the degree and leading term of a product, and in complete-square mode to build a canonical form (x^2 + bx as a square missing its corner (b/2)^2).
components.student_action: type a monomial in a cell, tap same-degree cells to collect them, type the unknown coefficients degree by degree; in complete-square mode read the missing corner and write a(x - alpha)^2 + beta
components.engine_needs: new src/engine/polynomial.ts: exact polynomials over rationals and simple surds (sqrt5, sqrt3), expansion and collection by degree, coefficient comparison, solving the triangular identification system (m, n, p, then the check on the last coefficient), canonical form with exact alpha and beta; cells checked by sample equivalence through the safe parser
components.props_sketch: left, right (lists of terms, unknown coefficients allowed), target (polynomial to match), mode: expand | identify | degree | complete_square, unknowns, givenCells

components.name: BoundsRuler
components.purpose: A zoomable graduated ruler for encadrements and approximations: a bracket a < x < b is pushed through the operations of the question (subtract 2, square a positive, multiply by 600, take 1/x of a positive) and the student sees the new bracket, then whether it decides a rounding (does it straddle the half-way mark?) or gives an approximation par defaut / par exces at 10^-n.
components.student_action: tap the operation to apply, drag or type the new bounds, tap 'arrondi = ...' or 'on ne peut pas conclure'; zoom one decimal further
components.engine_needs: new src/engine/bounds.ts: exact rational interval arithmetic for monotone operations (+c, x k with the sign rule, x^2 and sqrt on positives, 1/x on positives), the rounding decision at 10^-n (nearest, par defaut, par exces, unit above), the true value (surd or rational) placed to check every bracket; a bracket that does not contain the true value is refused
components.props_sketch: start {lower, upper, of}, ops [{kind: add | mul | square | sqrt | inv, by}], target {expr, decimals, mode: nearest | default | excess | ceil}, ticks, zoomLevels

notes_by_year.1s: beyond the 2eme spec (par defaut / par exces, rounding): the 1ere 'valeur approchee a 10^p pres' test (both 0.64 and 0.65 approximate 9/14 to 10^-2), a compare target that may answer 'the bracket cannot decide' (21.21 < 15 sqrt 2 < 21.225 against 21.22), and a start given as an inequality on an expression (-1 <= 2x - 3 <= 1/2) pushed back to x

components.name: DivisibilityChecker
components.purpose: An integer written digit by digit with a divisor's criterion lit (units digit for 2 and 5, last two digits for 4 and 25, last three for 8, digit sum for 3 and 9, S1 - S2 by rank from the right for 11 with the manual's d + 11p rule) and the remainder it gives; unknown digits as slots (4c17, 6a3b, xyz) the student tries; a list filter (two-digit endings divisible by 4 using allowed digits).
components.student_action: tap a divisor to light its criterion and type the remainder; try a digit in a slot and see if the condition holds; strike the numbers of a list that fail
components.engine_needs: arithmetic.ts: remainders by 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 25 through the criterion and by direct division (both must agree), rank parity from the right, the d + 11p rule for a negative d, every digit value satisfying a set of conditions (enumeration over 0-9 per slot), the symbolic criterion for letter digits (d = x + z - y)
components.props_sketch: number (digits or letter slots), divisors, ask: divisible | remainder | find_digits {conditions} | filter {list, conditions}, showCriterion

notes_by_year.1s: beyond the 2eme spec (criteria, digit slots, filters): a division mode a = bq + r with 0 <= r < b (500 = 12 x 41 + 8 -> 41 multiples of 12 up to 500), a remainder-pattern row (18k mod 12 for k = 1..6), the Euclid chain (1176, 756 -> 84), and a long-division mode that lists the remainders, lights the first one that repeats and gives the n-th digit (9/14 = 0.6428571..., 100th digit 8)

components.engine_needs: new src/engine/arithmetic.ts: factorisation of integers up to a few million, divisor check, exponents, largest square factor (n = k^2 m, m square-free), 'is a power of b'; PGCD / PPCM from factorisations (1ere)
